prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System: Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell; Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport retain local/statutory authority. Aliases: Airline Operations Coordinator=Saffron; Regional Flow Manager=Copperfin; Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone; Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard; Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove; Tower Supervisor=Brindle(section-only drills); Ramp Control Lead=Quartzline(voice/chat); Slot Allocation Engine=Blueharbor(transition-training controller references). Airline Operations Centre→Airline Interface Adapter→Flight Data Exchange: Flight Intent Message(route/timing/registration/turnaround/crew/connections); Identity Access Service authenticates; Business Rules Registry maps carriers/fairness; invalid/incomplete rejected(reason-codes); material intents supersede schedules; changes require messages. Saffron maintains readiness/constraints/legality. Marlinstone demand+Capacity Assessment Module constraints→Blueharbor; inputs: intents, Airport Capacity Plan, Airport Acceptance Rate, runway-metering limits, sector-loading. Blueharbor→Adapter/Foxglove: Calculated Takeoff Time/Target Off Block Time/arrival-opportunities. Ground Delay Program preserves capacity before preferences. Priority: authority-validated safety/emergency/humanitarian/national-obligation; scheduled commercial(timetable/readiness/capacity/fairness); general-aviation/repositioning/training/discretionary unless justified. Copperfin owns priority-policy, authorizes Capacity Reduction State exceptions/baseline/recovery/divergence; Slot Coordinator administers/reviews/confirms publication. Fairness: delay-distribution/proportional-access/no-systematic-disadvantage; excessive transferred delay requires visible,logged rule. Adapter preferences advisory; off-block readiness failures permit resequencing. Orchard validates weather/provenance/overrides; Storm Cell Snapshot qualifies confidence; degradation visible; uncertain capacity provisional; timestamped updates mandatory. Meteorology Briefing Officer interprets. Time Synchronization Service→Audit Event Ledger timestamps; Alert Distribution Hub distributes approvals. East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor→Ramp Movement Board→Surface Surveillance Adapter→Foxglove: advisory movements; Quartzline reconciles evidence. Tower Supervisor/Airport Duty Manager resolve conflicts; Runway Inspection Note precedes capacity endorsement; confirmed positions trigger recalculation; North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter receive capacities. Quartzline sends Stand Tow Request Form; prioritizes

New part:
S237: The Airline Operations Coordinator uses the delay slip when requesting an exemption review for a crew connectivity constraint that is not already represented in the allocation data.
S238: Exemption requests are evaluated against safety impact, network impact, passenger impact, crew legality, and the availability of a lower-impact alternative.
S239: The Slot Coordinator records each accepted or rejected exemption in the Collaborative Decision Log with the rule applied, the approving role, and the expected operational consequence.
S240: The Data Governance Steward ensures that exemption categories, priority codes, and fairness metrics are versioned in the Business Rules Registry before they are used in live allocation.
S241: The Arrival Regulation Console presents proposed arrival opportunities with the capacity source, regulation start time, and expected delay for each affected flight.
S242: The Departure Metering Service presents proposed departure opportunities and associated Calculated Takeoff Time values for coordination with the Tower Sequence Manager.
S243: The Tower Supervisor may reject a proposed departure opportunity when runway safety, wake spacing, or local sequencing conditions make the proposal impracticable.
S244: The Ramp Control Lead may identify apron constraints through the Ramp Movement Board, but the Slot Allocation Engine remains responsible for recalculating the regulated opportunity.
S245: All allocation runs are time stamped by the Time Synchronization Service and written to the Audit Event Ledger for later reconstruction of the decision sequence.
S246: During Normal Operations, allocation results are refreshed at regular intervals, while Adverse Weather Mode and Recovery Phase allow shorter recalculation cycles approved by the Regional Flow Manager.
S247: If the Regional Flow Platform enters Contingency Fallback State, the Contingency Operations Console preserves the last valid allocation, supports manual amendments, and marks the resulting Slot Compliance State as provisional.
S248: Post-event assessment in the Performance Analytics Warehouse compares proposed opportunities, actual movement times, exemption usage, and operator-level delay equity to improve subsequent rule calibration.
S249: Collaborative target time management establishes a shared operating baseline for each departure by linking the Target Off Block Time, the Calculated Takeoff Time, and the key surface milestone timestamps to the same flight record.
S250: The Regional Flow Platform creates the initial Target Off Block Time proposal from current flight intent, stand readiness, turnaround progress, and applicable airport capacity constraints.
S251: The Demand Prediction Service estimates demand pressure over the next planning horizon and marks flights whose proposed Target Off Block Time values are likely to cause runway or sector imbalance.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
